The council recommends making Silver certification compulsory for projects on plots exceeding 5,000 square metres. It also seeks property tax concessions for certified residential buildings to encourage developer participation.

The proposed projects will also cover Dronacharya temple in Greater Noida and Radha Kund

stories.title: Telangana plans climate-resilient urban infrastructure
stories.summary: Telangana is implementing a climate-resilience plan backed by a 20,000 crore rupee project pipeline. The roadmap includes bamboo bus shelters, waste dump reclamation and a mandatory Urban Road Code. These measures are part of the state's long-term vision to integrate climate concerns into municipal services and urban planning.

stories.title: Kochi Metro secures co-branding for all stations
stories.summary: Kochi Metro Rail Ltd has become the first network in India to secure semi-naming rights for all 25 stations on its Blue line. The initiative aims to boost non-ticket revenue by adding brand names to station signage. The company expects to generate 100 percent branding revenue from its stations.

stories.title: Max Estates acquires Noida land for mixed-use development
stories.summary: Max Estates has purchased a 5.5-acre land parcel in Noida for 272 crore rupees through an e-auction. The company plans to develop a mixed-use project as part of its regional expansion. Forty percent of the bid value is payable within 60 days of the authority's allotment.

stories.title: HSBC sub-leases office space in Bengaluru
stories.summary: HSBC Electronic Data Processing India has sub-leased 1.19 lakh sq ft of office space at Bengaluru's Ecospace Campus. The five-year deal is valued at over 207 crore rupees, according to property registration documents. The office is fully furnished.

stories.title: DLF to invest in IREO group companies
stories.summary: DLF plans to invest approximately 3,750 crore rupees in a joint venture with Everstone Group. The partnership aims to acquire an aggregate economic interest of about 40 percent in IREO India companies. The two firms have signed a binding and exclusive term sheet.

stories.title: DLF and Everstone Group announce joint venture
stories.summary: DLF has announced a 3,750 crore rupee joint venture with Singapore-headquartered Everstone Group. The investment will secure a majority stake in a vehicle holding economic interests in IREO India companies. The arrangement involves funds from several global investors.

stories.title: Thiruvananthapuram reviews Smart City infrastructure
stories.summary: Thiruvananthapuram is conducting a physical assessment of 81 projects completed under the Smart City Mission. Launched in 2016 with a 1,538 crore rupee outlay, many facilities remain non-functional or underutilised. The new administration has decided to restart the handover process for the completed works.

stories.title: MCD suspends engineers following building collapse
stories.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has suspended two engineers after a building collapse killed two people. A preliminary inquiry found the owner continued construction under the guise of repair work despite an earlier inspection. The corporation had previously issued an advisory against such activity.

stories.title: University of Miami to curate U.S. Pavilion
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of State selected the University of Miami School of Architecture to curate the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale pavilion. Lead curator Germane Barnes and historian Vyta Pivo will present Earth Craft, an exhibition exploring building materials like brick, rammed earth, adobe, and concrete masonry.

stories.title: University of Miami selected for Venice Biennale
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of State has chosen the University of Miami School of Architecture to organize the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale pavilion. Titled Earth Craft, the exhibition traces earthen materials from the ground to finished buildings, honouring the communities of brickmakers and masons who shape them.

stories.title: Curators announced for U.S. Pavilion in Venice
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of State announced that the University of Miami School of Architecture will represent the country at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale. The exhibition, Earth Craft, will explore the history and labor behind materials including brick, rammed earth, and adobe.

stories.title: Shortlist announced for Sydney waterfront project
stories.summary: Six design teams have been shortlisted for the redevelopment of Sydney's Bays West precinct. The project aims to transform the waterfront into a residential suburb featuring up to 8,500 homes. At least 10 percent of the housing is designated for affordable and essential worker use.

stories.title: Shortlist announced for Sydney waterfront project
stories.summary: Six design teams have been shortlisted for the redevelopment of Sydney's Bays West precinct. The project aims to transform the waterfront into a residential suburb featuring up to 8,500 homes. At least 10 percent of the housing is designated for affordable and essential worker use.

stories.title: JSWD wins design contract for Riyadh towers
stories.summary: German architecture firm JSWD has won an international design competition to develop the RIYMAR Towers. The project is a major mixed-use real estate development planned for Riyadh. Further details on the design are available via the project website.

stories.title: Architecture Research Office completes park pavilion
stories.summary: New York-based studio Architecture Research Office has completed a green-roofed pavilion at Providence's 195 District Park. The structure features an aluminium canopy and serves as a year-round amenity for the public. It includes indoor-outdoor dining space and restrooms overlooking the Providence River.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta museum opens in Sydney
stories.summary: Powerhouse Parramatta opens to the public on November 7. Designed by Moreau Kusunoki and Genton, the museum features a steel lattice exoskeleton. The inaugural program includes five exhibitions with immersive installations by artists including Es Devlin and James Turrell.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta museum set to open
stories.summary: The Powerhouse Parramatta museum in Sydney is scheduled to open tomorrow. Described as the largest cultural project in Australia since the Sydney Opera House, the building is wrapped in a lattice exoskeleton. The museum aims to pioneer a new model for contemporary museum practice.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta opens amid controversy
stories.summary: Powerhouse Parramatta opens this weekend with a 915 million dollar price tag. The project has faced years of criticism from former staff and trustees who argue the museum shifted focus away from its core business. The building is dubbed the Opera House of western Sydney.

stories.title: Zaha Hadid Foundation commissions video installation
stories.summary: The Zaha Hadid Foundation has commissioned a video installation by artist LionHeart to mark the tenth anniversary of the architect's death. Titled The Rebar Beneath, the work uses film and poetry to explore the relationship between visible surfaces and the structures that shape space.

stories.title: Blue Origin unveils 3D-printed Northstar engine
stories.summary: Blue Origin has unveiled Northstar, a liquefied natural gas engine rated at 715,000 pounds of thrust. The company claims the engine is stronger, lighter and features 30 percent less mass and half the parts of its predecessor. More than 65 percent of the unit is 3D-printed in-house.

stories.title: Blue Origin targets 1,000 launches per year
stories.summary: Blue Origin announced upgrades to its New Glenn rocket to reduce manufacturing costs and increase payload capacity. CEO Dave Limp stated the company aims to eventually launch more than 1,000 times a year. The company has begun test firing its new Northstar engine to replace the current BE-4.

stories.title: Western Cape introduces 3D-printed spinal braces
stories.summary: The Western Cape Department of Health and Wellness has launched a 3D scanning and printing service for spinal braces at its Orthotic and Prosthetic Centre. The technology reduces patient waiting times from two weeks to two days. Six patients have received braces following a R5.5 million equipment investment.

stories.title: Western Cape expands 3D-printed medical support
stories.summary: The Western Cape Department of Health and Wellness is using 3D printing to produce spinal braces for patients with scoliosis or injuries. MEC Mireille Wenger called the technology a game changer for reducing wait times from two weeks to two days. Early bracing aims to prevent progressive spine curvature.

stories.title: Pre-painted aluminum market shifts to 2035
stories.summary: The global pre-painted aluminum sheets market enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement and a regionally diversified supply architecture, according to an IndexBox report. These materials are valued for corrosion resistance and longevity. The industry is currently shaped by stringent environmental regulations and energy efficiency requirements for building and automotive sectors.

stories.title: Bamboo charcoal market expands beyond household use
stories.summary: The bamboo charcoal market is growing as industrial buyers seek adsorbents that can be described in one line on a label. Producers are investing in carbonization technology to supply charcoal for facial masks, soaps, textiles and filtration. The material traps odors and pollutants without added chemicals or fragrance.

stories.title: ANDRITZ supports India's first bamboo-based ethanol plant
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. The Asia Pacific Sustainable Aviation Centre and ISCC have signed a memorandum of understanding to support sustainable aviation fuel supply chains. Meanwhile, LanzaJet has secured at least $20 million in new financing to scale its alcohol-to-jet fuel technology and accelerate commercial production.

stories.title: New study targets photorealistic BIM reconstructions
stories.summary: A study in Multimedia Tools and Applications addresses the plain appearance of as-built building information models. Authors Yuyang Jin, Siyi Li, Lihui Huang, Nanying Liang and Yiyu Cai introduced a method to convert laser scans into photorealistic models, aiming to improve visual interpretability and automated defect detection in construction.

stories.title: Singapore pushes embodied AI in construction
stories.summary: Singapore is integrating embodied AI into its construction sector to address labor constraints and productivity challenges. Unlike conventional systems, embodied AI connects intelligence to physical machines, allowing robots to perceive surroundings and perform precision tasks. The country is accelerating efforts to modernize the industry through robotics and automation.

stories.title: Architectural theory on environmental management
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Architectural historian Reyner Banham argued that buildings are complex systems negotiating the relationship between occupants and their surroundings. He identified conservative and selective strategies for environmental management, challenging the assumption that architecture focuses primarily on form and enclosure rather than heating, cooling and lighting.

stories.title: Chaos adds AI tools to V-Ray Collection
stories.summary: Chaos has updated its V-Ray Collection with AI-focused features, including 3D asset generation and an integrated assistant for settings analysis. Users can now connect external AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT via Model Context Protocol servers to automate time-consuming tasks within their 3D visualisation workflows.

stories.title: India launches pilot for heat-resilient cities
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has launched a strategic pilot programme under AMRUT 2.0 to help cities address urban heat risks. Twelve cities are receiving funding to implement pilot projects and identify innovative solutions for vulnerable communities. The programme focuses on city-level interventions and adaptive strategies.

stories.title: Agartala reviews smart city sewage progress
stories.summary: Tripura’s Chief Secretary chaired a high-level meeting to accelerate sewage network upgrades under the Agartala Smart City Project. The review focused on expediting infrastructure work before upcoming municipal polling. Timely progress is intended to address drainage concerns and strengthen sanitation facilities across the city.

stories.title: Maharashtra plans restoration of historic stepwells
stories.summary: Maharashtra is planning to restore 75 historic stepwells, locally known as baravs, to combat recurring drought. The government hopes to repurpose this traditional water infrastructure for modern use. The first phase of the initiative involves an investment of Rs 25 crore by the Cultural Affairs Department.

stories.title: Delhi pollution report sparks construction questions
stories.summary: A report citing an AQI of 687 claims a construction ban was imposed in Delhi from 5 to 20 November. The report does not identify the issuing authority or provide official notification text. The figures and the status of the restriction remain unconfirmed by official sources.

stories.title: Construction continues despite NCR ban
stories.summary: Despite a CAQM-mandated construction halt, work continued at public and private sites across the NCR on the first day of the restriction. Contractors reported accelerating work due to fears of further limitations. Dust mitigation measures remained largely absent, leaving major stretches of the region in a grey haze.

stories.title: BNHS publishes Mammals of India
stories.summary: The Bombay Natural History Society has published Mammals of India, authored by A.J.T. Johnsingh and P.O. Nameer. The book, which began development in 2018, aims to serve both wildlife researchers and non-expert readers. It documents India’s mammalian biodiversity following a collaboration with Harper Collins Publishers India.

stories.title: Great Indian Bustard rewilding programme faces losses
stories.summary: India has released four captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the wild, though one was predated within days. Scientists estimate post-release survival at 30 percent. The programme faces questions regarding its predator management approach and overall transparency as it attempts to revive the critically-endangered species.

stories.title: Nijmegen moves dikes to manage flood risk
stories.summary: Nijmegen moved the Lent dike inland by 350 meters and excavated a 3-kilometer channel to expand flood drainage space. The project follows the Netherlands' Room for the River program, which shifted focus from raising dikes to creating more room for water to flow during heavy rains.

stories.title: Professor urges green spaces to curb urban heat
stories.summary: Professor John Kusimi has called on municipal assemblies to encourage greener property development to reduce flooding and heat. He says paving residential compounds with concrete and bitumen prevents rainwater from seeping into the ground, which increases surface runoff and puts pressure on existing urban drainage systems.

stories.title: Lo Lo Chai Village balances tourism and tradition
stories.summary: Lo Lo Chai Village faces a paradox where preservation attracts tourists but development threatens its character. Concrete houses mimicking ancient rammed earth walls are now crowding the village. The world's best tourist village is currently working to ensure that modern development does not stifle its traditional identity.

stories.title: Vietnam green building market continues to grow
stories.summary: The International Finance Corporation reports that Vietnam will have 780 green-certified buildings by the end of 2025. These projects prioritize energy efficiency and green spaces to improve resident health. The market is expected to continue its growth through 2026 as green buildings become a new standard.

stories.title: Cities remain part of natural systems
stories.summary: Cities often appear to be the opposite of nature, yet they rely on natural systems for water, food, and energy. Waste and wastewater leave toward other places, and urban areas contain their own ecosystems of trees, parks, and wildlife. A city is still part of Earth.

stories.title: SWA deploys toolkit for walkable Houston
stories.summary: Landscape architecture studio SWA is implementing a modular system of architectural elements and mesh canopies to retrofit Houston streets. The Cool and Connected Corridors project aims to make the urban streetscape more delightful and comfortable, as part of the city's wider Public Realm Action Plan initiative.

stories.title: Philippines pilots nature-based coastal protection
stories.summary: The Philippines is using bamboo poles, tree branches, and oyster shells to reduce wave energy and trap sediment on Pamarawan Island. This nature-based model aims to combat rising sea levels and storm-driven waves without relying entirely on the traditional concrete sea walls and embankments used elsewhere.

stories.title: Researchers test wave-shaped building designs
stories.summary: FAMU-FSU researchers are using 3D-printed models and wind tunnels to test wave-shaped roofs and walls. The team says these designs could cut wind pressure by up to 60 percent. The unusual geometry is intended to help Florida homes withstand the force of hurricane-strength winds.

stories.title: Hurricane-proof library opens in Miami
stories.summary: Designed by 89th Studio, Le Petite Bibliothèque is a 264-square-foot civic shelter in North Miami. The structure houses an automated 24-hour lending kiosk and is wrapped in high-velocity polycarbonate paneling to protect the facility from hurricane-force winds. The library is designed to remain resilient during storms.

stories.title: Task force rethinks residential rebuilding
stories.summary: The SCI-Arc Resilient Futures Task Force was formed after 2025 wildfires exposed weaknesses in Southern California building standards. The group provides displaced homeowners with practical help regarding safety codes and insurance claims. The initiative aims to avoid repeating past construction mistakes as wildfires become more frequent.

stories.title: Teens assist resident during flooding
stories.summary: A resident whose home was flooding received help from a group of teenagers who saw her request for assistance on social media. The group arrived to provide aid during the event.

stories.title: Super El Niño expected to peak in December
stories.summary: A rapidly developing super El Niño is forecast to peak at the end of 2026. Carbon Brief analysis suggests this will push average global temperatures to record levels next year. Dr. Zeke Hausfather described the current climate pattern as simply staggering in a recent update.

stories.title: UN climate summit faces modest expectations
stories.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya begins with governments pulled between short-term national interests and the need for collective action. While renewable energy is a priority, prospects for significant progress remain modest. Developing countries continue to seek greater finance and support to adapt to ongoing climate damage.

stories.title: Security deployment deepens dam project tensions
stories.summary: Protests against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh have led to arrests and a heavy security presence. The state government views the dam as a safeguard against upstream projects, while residents fear the loss of their land. Negotiations remain stalled until detained protesters are released.

stories.title: Appeals court clears way for pied-à-terre tax
stories.summary: An appeals court ruled that the rollout of New York City's pied-à-terre tax can proceed. The decision reversed a lower court's previous ruling that had found the initial notices sent to homeowners were flawed.

stories.title: Voters decide on state housing policies
stories.summary: California, Hawaiʻi, and Rhode Island have approved new housing bond policies. However, proposed permitting and zoning changes in California and Massachusetts remain undecided following the recent ballot. The status of these housing policies varies by state.

stories.title: Generative Bionics plans AI data factory
stories.summary: Generative Bionics is planning a network of Physical AI Data Factories, starting with a 5,000-square-metre hub in Italy. The facility is designed to connect real-world robot learning and data processing. The company describes the initiative as a strategic plan to build a three-node network.

stories.title: BIM Capital and Axelerated Solutions launch fund
stories.summary: BIM Capital and Axelerated Solutions have launched a $180 million fund dedicated to AI data centres. The investment aims to support the infrastructure required for artificial intelligence operations. Further details on the fund's specific allocations are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Europe data center market projected to reach USD 52.64 billion
stories.summary: Arizton reports the European sustainable data center market will grow from USD 13.47 billion in 2025 to USD 52.64 billion by 2031. Developers are facing pressure to secure renewable power and improve cooling efficiency as AI-driven capacity requirements increase. The region is currently reshaping its infrastructure priorities.

stories.title: Physicl raises $10 million for robot training
stories.summary: Physicl has closed a $10 million funding round to improve simulated training environments for robots. The startup repurposes e-commerce technology to create digital twins, aiming to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world performance. The goal is to ensure robots do not fumble when they hit the real world.

stories.title: URobotics secures $30 million for autonomous mobility
stories.summary: Physical AI startup URobotics raised USD 30 million in a Series A round led by Kiwoom Investment and K2 Investment Partners. The company develops modular autonomous mobility kits for robots, including humanoids and quadrupeds. The product is designed to function in complex environments without being tied to specific hardware.

stories.summary: The University of Bath has broken ground on a 926-bed student housing project designed to Passivhaus standards. The development uses a fabric-first approach and air source heat pumps to reduce operational carbon. It is intended to house every first-year undergraduate on campus by the time it completes in 2028.

stories.title: Liverpool School of Architecture opens new building
stories.summary: The University of Liverpool has officially opened its new architecture school building. The facility includes virtual reality suites, digital design spaces, and collaborative work areas for students and researchers. The opening ceremony was led by actor and architecture alumnus Anton Lesser, marking a new era for the school.

stories.summary: Architecture Professor Lawrence Davis and alumnus Chenhao Luo earned an honorable mention in The Next House: USA competition. The proposal aimed to reimagine the American suburban home as an affordable and adaptable space. The competition challenged designers to address rising housing costs and changing household needs.

stories.title: University of Minnesota architecture prototypes on Nicollet Mall
stories.summary: The University of Minnesota School of Architecture has installed design prototypes on Nicollet Mall. The project, titled Nicollet Next, showcases work from the school. The full details of the installation and the associated design goals are available to subscribers of the Star Tribune.

stories.title: Georgia Tech researcher joins White House Fellowship
stories.summary: Former Georgia Tech research faculty member Kyle Saleeby has been selected for the 2026-27 class of White House Fellows. Saleeby will work with the National Security Council on advanced manufacturing and supply chains. The White House describes the program as an opportunity for gifted and motivated Americans.

stories.title: Yasmeen Lari discusses architectural practice
stories.summary: Yasmeen Lari, the 2023 RIBA Royal Gold Medallist, discussed her shift from conventional practice to building with bamboo, mud and lime. Speaking at the in:situ 2026 conference, she addressed the role of architects and the goal of making one's own professional practice redundant.

research.title: A clever molecular trick unlocks previously impossible properties in glass
research.summary: Scientists have discovered how to reprogram the internal structure of glass using a special molecule that rearranges chemical bonds while lowering the melting temperature. The breakthrough could unlock entirely new glass materials with precisely controlled magnetic and optical properties, opening possibilities for advanced electronics, sensors, and other technologies.

research.title: Scientists discover that a clogged filter could revolutionize oil refining
research.summary: Scientists have developed a remarkable new membrane that separates crude oil at room temperature, using the oil itself to create microscopic filtration channels. research.title: MIT scientists break a 20-year rule and unlock never-before-seen crystal structures
research.summary: MIT scientists have challenged two decades of conventional thinking by discovering that flexible molecular connections, rather than rigid ones, can unlock entirely new ways to arrange nanoparticles. The breakthrough could lead to a new generation of designer materials with unusual properties and applications in electronics, medicine, and energy.

research.title: Large Hadron Collider reveals evidence of Big Bang matter in surprisingly small collisions
research.summary: Scientists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have uncovered compelling new evidence that even relatively small atomic collisions can recreate the extraordinary state of matter that filled the universe moments after the Big Bang. Known as quark-gluon plasma, this exotic substance forms at temperatures more than 100,000 times hotter.

research.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
research.summary: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.

research.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
research.summary: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. research.title: Scientists say a forgotten particle may explain why the universe exists
research.summary: A mysterious particle overlooked for decades may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang, allowing stars, planets, and life to exist. Scientists believe this forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have left detectable gravitational wave signals that could help unlock the cosmos’s deepest.

research.title: Scientists shrink Archimedes’ screw to the size of a single molecule
research.summary: Scientists have built a groundbreaking molecular motor that spins in either direction using electricity, inspired by a machine invented more than 2,000 years ago. Even more remarkably, its rotation can boost electrical conductivity by up to 100 times, potentially transforming the future of molecular electronics.
